# Kosambiya Sutta (MN 48 (PTS MN i 320))

**ID:** MN 48 (PTS MN i 320)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Kosambiya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 320
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosambiya Sutta* (MN 48) is set at Ghosita's Park near Kosambī, where the resident monastic community had fallen into bitter internal dissension, quarrelling and assailing one another with verbal daggers [Granoff; IBC 2011; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995]. In response to this breach of concord, the Buddha intervenes to teach the monks six memorable qualities that create love, respect, and unity, reminding them of the peaceful state they seek [Hazra 1994; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003].

The commentary glosses this *dhammatā* as *sabhāva* ("inherent nature") [Cousins et al. 1974].

The dispute at Kosambī is also well known from the Vinaya literature—such as the Pali *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Vin Kd 10) and the Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda *Kośāmbīvastu*—as well as the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128) [Granoff; Rogell 2003].

**Sources**

- [Cousins et al. 1974] L. Cousins, A. Kunst, and K. R. Norman (eds.), Buddhist Studies in Honour of I.B. Horner (1974) — Discussion of dhammatā, stream-enterers confessing offenses, and the commentary's gloss
- [IBC 2011] 8th International Buddhist Conference, Buddhist Virtues in Socio-Economic Development (2011) — Citations of the Kosambī dispute and quoting the opening canonical formula
- [Granoff] Phyllis Granoff, Regionalism in Vinaya — Context on the internal disputes of the Kauśāmbī monks in the sutta and Vinaya traditions
- [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi (trans.), The Middle Length Discourses of the Buddha (1995) — English titles, setting at Ghosita's Park, six qualities of unity, and seven knowledges of stream-entry
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Summary of MN 48 dealing with Kosambī disputes and amity
- [Rogell 2003] Sharda Rogell, Pressing Out Pure Honey: A Practitioner's Study Guide (Majjhima Nikāya) (2003) — Teaching on the six qualities, right view, seven knowledges, and connection to MN 128
